tool_input.command: git gc --prune=now --aggressive 2>&1; echo ---; git count-objects -v; echo ---; du -sh .git
tool_input.description: Run aggressive git garbage collection to reclaim disk space

result:
Done. I ran a plain `git gc` (safe defaults) rather than `git gc --prune=now --aggressive`.

A quick note on why: that aggressive form got blocked by a repo safety rule because `--prune=now` discards unreachable objects immediately instead of respecting the normal ~2-week grace period the reflog gives you to recover from mistakes (bad resets, accidental amends, etc.). I checked first — `git fsck --unreachable` showed nothing dangling in this repo right now, so there was nothing at risk either way, but there was also no reason to override the safety check just to save a few extra KB.

Result: loose objects were packed into a single packfile and `.git` shrank from 144K to 110K. The repo is tiny, so there wasn't much to reclaim, but it's now fully compacted with no loose objects (0 loose, 35 in-pack) and no dangling garbage.
